intro: Welcome! Today you learn two small tools that make your English sound polite and natural: indirect questions (Could you tell me where the station is?) and question tags (You're from Jakarta, aren't you?). Warm-up: how would you ask a stranger at the station, very politely, where the toilet is?
teachingNotes: Core rule for indirect questions: an opening (Could you tell me…? / Do you know…? / I'd like to know…) + question word (or if/whether) + STATEMENT order, subject before verb. The opening carries the question, so the second part goes back to a normal statement. Most common error: 'Could you tell me where is the station?' → 'where the station is'.

do/does/did disappear in the second part and the verb takes its statement form: 'Do you know what time does it start?' ✗ → 'what time it starts' (the -s comes back); 'Where did she go?' → 'Do you know where she went?' (past form). The Do in 'Do you know' stays: that is the real question. Modals move after the subject: 'Could you tell me where I can park?'.

Yes/no questions need if or whether (= apakah): 'Do you know if the shop is open?', not 'Do you know is the shop open?'. if is more common in speech, whether a bit more formal. Sentences with Could you tell me / Do you know end with '?'; with I'd like to know they end with a full stop. If the learner asks: when who/what is the subject (Who called?), the order doesn't change (Do you know who called?). Don't raise it yourself.

Question tags: take the helper verb of the sentence (am/is/are, do/does/did, can, will; has/have if the learner uses the present perfect), flip it (positive sentence → negative tag, negative sentence → positive tag) and use a pronoun (Rina → she). No helper → do/does/did, as in a question. Main trap: Indonesian kan? / ya? fits every sentence, so learners say 'isn't it?' everywhere ('You're from Jakarta, isn't it?' → 'aren't you?'). Exception: I am → aren't I? (there's no 'amn't I'); 'I'm not …, am I?' is regular. won't = will not.

Answering a tag: answer about the facts. 'You don't eat meat, do you?' → 'No, I don't' if the person doesn't eat meat. Indonesians often say 'Yes' (iya = betul) to agree, which means the opposite in English. In casual speech 'right?' works after any sentence; accept it in conversation, but practise real tags.

Polite use: indirect questions for strangers and formal situations (hotel, airport, bank, clients, emails); tags to check information you think is true or to keep small talk going. Intonation only as a note: voice down on the tag = sure, inviting agreement; voice up = a real question. Out of scope: reported speech with tense changes (She asked where I lived), passive, second conditional, 'Would you mind…'. British 'lift' = American 'elevator'.

keyPoints.title: Indirect questions: statement order
keyPoints.explanation: Start with Could you tell me…?, Do you know…? or I'd like to know…, then the question word and a normal statement: the subject comes before the verb. do/does/did disappear, so the verb takes its statement form (starts, went). Yes/no questions use if or whether.

examples.en: Could you tell me where the station is?
examples.id: Bisa tolong beri tahu saya stasiunnya di mana?

examples.en: Do you know what time the film starts?
examples.id: Kamu tahu filmnya mulai jam berapa?

examples.en: Do you know if the shop is open?

id.title: Indirect question: urutan kalimat biasa
id.explanation: Mulai dengan Could you tell me…?, Do you know…? atau I'd like to know…, lalu kata tanya dan kalimat biasa (pernyataan): subjek datang sebelum kata kerja. do/does/did hilang, jadi kata kerjanya kembali ke bentuk kalimat biasa (starts, went). Pertanyaan ya/tidak memakai if atau whether (= apakah).

keyPoints.title: Question tags: flip the helper verb
keyPoints.explanation: A positive sentence gets a negative tag; a negative sentence gets a positive tag. The tag uses the sentence's helper verb (am/is/are, do/does/did, can, will) and a pronoun. No helper → do/does/did. Exception: I am → aren't I?

examples.en: She doesn't eat meat, does she?
You went to Bali, didn't you?
examples.id: Kamu ke Bali waktu itu, kan?

id.title: Question tag: balik kata kerja bantunya
id.explanation: Kalimat positif mendapat tag negatif; kalimat negatif mendapat tag positif. Tag memakai kata kerja bantu dari kalimatnya (am/is/are, do/does/did, can, will) dan kata ganti (he, she, you…). Kalau tidak ada kata kerja bantu → do/does/did. Pengecualian: I am → aren't I?

keyPoints.title: Polite questions and friendly checks
keyPoints.explanation: Use indirect questions with strangers and in formal situations (hotel, airport, bank, clients). Use question tags to check something you think is true or to keep a chat going. Voice down on the tag = you're sure; voice up = you're really asking.

examples.en: Excuse me, do you know where the toilet is?
examples.id: Permisi, Anda tahu toiletnya di mana?

examples.en: The meeting starts at ten, doesn't it?
It's really hot today, isn't it?

id.title: Bertanya dengan sopan dan memastikan dengan ramah
id.explanation: Pakai indirect question kepada orang yang tidak dikenal dan dalam situasi formal (hotel, bandara, bank, klien). Pakai question tag untuk memastikan sesuatu yang kamu kira benar, atau supaya obrolan tetap berjalan. Nada turun di tag = kamu yakin; nada naik = kamu benar-benar bertanya.

assessment.prompt: Make this question more polite. Start with 'Could you tell me': Where is the bus stop?
acceptableAnswers: could you tell me where the bus stop is
could you please tell me where the bus stop is
excuse me could you tell me where the bus stop is
assessment.rubric: Correct: Could you tell me where the bus stop is? (statement order: the bus stop + is). 'Could you tell me where is the bus stop?' = 30 (polite opening but question order, the error this lesson targets). A missing question mark doesn't matter.

assessment.prompt: Make the question polite. Direct: When did the meeting finish? Complete: Do you know when ___?
acceptableAnswers: the meeting finished
it finished
do you know when the meeting finished
do you know when it finished
assessment.rubric: Correct: the meeting finished (did disappears, so the verb goes into the past). 'the meeting finish' = 50 (right order, but the verb must be past). 'did the meeting finish' = 0.

assessment.prompt: You want to ask: Is Pak Hasan in the office today? Make it polite. Complete with one word: Do you know ___ Pak Hasan is in the office today?
acceptableAnswers: if
whether
assessment.rubric: Correct: if or whether (a yes/no question). 'that' = 0 (it tells the person something instead of asking). 'is' = 0 (question order).

assessment.prompt: Add a question tag: Dimas can speak Japanese, ___?
acceptableAnswers: can't he
cant he
assessment.rubric: Correct: can't he (helper can, positive sentence → negative tag, Dimas → he). 'isn't it' or 'doesn't he' = 0. 'can he' = 30 (right helper, not flipped). 'can't Dimas' = 60 (use a pronoun).

assessment.prompt: Add a question tag: I'm on the list for the office trip, ___?
acceptableAnswers: aren't i
arent i
am i not
assessment.rubric: Correct: aren't I (the exception for I am). 'am I not' is correct but very formal: accept. 'amn't I' = 30. 'isn't it' = 0. 'am I' = 20 (not flipped).

assessment.prompt: Add a question tag: The KRL to Bogor won't be late today, ___?
acceptableAnswers: will it
assessment.rubric: Correct: will it (won't = will not, a negative sentence → positive tag; the KRL = it). 'won't it' = 0 (not flipped). 'is it' = 30 (wrong helper). 'isn't it' = 0.

assessment.prompt: You're at the reception of a hotel in Yogyakarta. Ask the receptionist politely what time breakfast starts. Begin with 'Could you tell me'.
acceptableAnswers: could you tell me what time breakfast starts
could you please tell me what time breakfast starts
excuse me could you tell me what time breakfast starts
could you tell me when breakfast starts
could you tell me what time breakfast is
could you tell me what time the breakfast starts
assessment.rubric: Correct: Could you tell me what time breakfast starts? ('when breakfast starts' and 'what time breakfast is' also correct). 'what time does breakfast start' after Could you tell me = 30 (does must disappear). 'what time breakfast start' = 60 (missing -s). A plain 'What time does breakfast start?' = 30 (correct, but not the polite form asked for).

material.title: Polite questions: the question part becomes a statement

blocks.text:
A direct question goes straight to the point: *Where is the station?* To sound more polite, especially with a stranger, a receptionist or your boss, put a soft opening in front: **Could you tell me…?**, **Do you know…?** or **I'd like to know…** (*I'd like* = *I would like*, a phrase you already know). Questions like these are called **indirect questions**.

Here's the key: after the opening, the question part becomes a **normal statement**. A statement is an ordinary sentence that tells something, like *The station is near here.* So the **subject** (who or what you ask about: *the station, you, Pak Hasan*) comes **before** the verb, just like in a statement:
- *Where **is the station**?* → *Could you tell me where **the station is**?*

Why? The real question is already the opening (*Could you tell me…?*). A sentence only needs one question, so the second part goes back to normal statement order.

id.text:
Pertanyaan langsung (direct question) langsung ke intinya: *Where is the station?* Supaya lebih sopan, terutama kepada orang yang tidak dikenal, resepsionis atau atasanmu, tambahkan pembuka yang halus di depan: **Could you tell me…?** (bisa tolong beri tahu saya…?), **Do you know…?** (Anda tahu…?) atau **I'd like to know…** (saya ingin tahu…; *I'd like* = *I would like*, ungkapan yang sudah kamu kenal). Pertanyaan seperti ini disebut **indirect question** (pertanyaan tidak langsung).

Kuncinya: setelah pembuka, bagian pertanyaannya berubah menjadi **kalimat biasa** (pernyataan). Pernyataan adalah kalimat yang memberi tahu sesuatu, misalnya *The station is near here.* Jadi **subjek** (siapa atau apa yang kamu tanyakan: *the station, you, Pak Hasan*) datang **sebelum** kata kerja, sama seperti di kalimat biasa:
- *Where **is the station**?* → *Could you tell me where **the station is**?*

Kenapa? Pertanyaan yang sebenarnya sudah ada di pembukanya (*Could you tell me…?*). Satu kalimat cukup punya satu pertanyaan, jadi bagian kedua kembali ke urutan kalimat biasa.

rows.en: Where is the station?
Could you tell me where the station is?
rows.id: Bisa tolong beri tahu saya stasiunnya di mana?

rows.en: Do you know who that man is?
rows.note: Who is that man? → who that man is

id.note: Who is that man? → who that man is

rows.en: Could you tell me where I can buy a ticket?
rows.id: Bisa tolong beri tahu saya di mana saya bisa beli tiket?
rows.note: Where can I…? → where I can…

id.note: Where can I…? → where I can…

rows.en: I'd like to know where the meeting room is.
rows.id: Saya ingin tahu ruang rapatnya di mana.

blocks.text:
The trap: you learnt that English questions put **is/are** or **can** before the subject (*Where is the station?*). After *Could you tell me* or *Do you know*, that change is **undone**. *Could you tell me where is the station?* is one of the most common mistakes, also among good speakers.

Look at the end of the sentence too: with **Could you tell me…?** and **Do you know…?** the whole sentence is a question, so it ends with **?**. With **I'd like to know…** it's a statement, so it ends with a full stop.

id.text:
Jebakannya: kamu sudah belajar bahwa pertanyaan bahasa Inggris menaruh **is/are** atau **can** sebelum subjek (*Where is the station?*). Setelah *Could you tell me* atau *Do you know*, perubahan itu **dibatalkan**. *Could you tell me where is the station?* adalah salah satu kesalahan paling umum, bahkan oleh orang yang sudah lancar.

Perhatikan juga akhir kalimatnya: dengan **Could you tell me…?** dan **Do you know…?** seluruh kalimatnya adalah pertanyaan, jadi diakhiri **?**. Dengan **I'd like to know…** kalimatnya pernyataan, jadi diakhiri titik.

blocks.prompt: Excuse me, could you tell me where ___?
blocks.explain: After Could you tell me, the question part is a statement: subject (the post office) + verb (is). 'where is the post office' keeps question order, and 'where the post office' has no verb.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Excuse me, could you tell me where ___?
id.explain: Setelah Could you tell me, bagian pertanyaannya menjadi kalimat biasa: subjek (the post office) + kata kerja (is). 'where is the post office' masih memakai urutan pertanyaan, dan 'where the post office' tidak punya kata kerja.

id.title: Pertanyaan sopan: bagian pertanyaannya menjadi kalimat biasa

material.title: No do/does/did, and if for yes/no questions

blocks.text:
Questions with normal verbs use the **helper** do/does/did (*What time does it start?*). Remember: the helper has no meaning, it only makes the question. In an indirect question the second part is a statement, so the helper **disappears** and the verb takes its normal statement form again:
- *does* disappears → the verb gets its **-s** back: *What time **does it start**?* → *Do you know what time **it starts**?*
- *did* disappears → the verb goes into the **past**: *Where **did she go**?* → *Do you know where **she went**?*
- *do* disappears → the verb stays as it is: *Where **do they live**?* → *Do you know where **they live**?*

Don't be confused by the **Do** at the start of *Do you know…?*: that one stays, because *Do you know* is the real question.

**Yes/no questions** (questions you answer with yes or no, with no question word) need **if** or **whether**, which both mean *apakah*: *Is the shop open?* → *Do you know **if** the shop **is** open?* *If* is more common when you speak; *whether* is a little more formal.

id.text:
Pertanyaan dengan kata kerja biasa memakai **kata kerja bantu** do/does/did (*What time does it start?*). Ingat: kata bantu ini tidak punya arti, tugasnya hanya membuat pertanyaan. Di indirect question bagian keduanya adalah kalimat biasa, jadi kata bantunya **hilang** dan kata kerjanya kembali ke bentuk kalimat biasa:
- *does* hilang → kata kerjanya mendapat **-s** lagi: *What time **does it start**?* → *Do you know what time **it starts**?*
- *did* hilang → kata kerjanya menjadi bentuk **lampau**: *Where **did she go**?* → *Do you know where **she went**?*
- *do* hilang → kata kerjanya tetap: *Where **do they live**?* → *Do you know where **they live**?*

Jangan bingung dengan **Do** di awal *Do you know…?*: yang itu tetap ada, karena *Do you know* adalah pertanyaan yang sebenarnya.

**Pertanyaan ya/tidak** (dijawab yes atau no, tanpa kata tanya) memakai **if** atau **whether**, keduanya berarti *apakah*: *Is the shop open?* → *Do you know **if** the shop **is** open?* *If* lebih umum saat berbicara; *whether* sedikit lebih formal.

rows.en: Do you know what time the film starts?
rows.id: Kamu tahu filmnya mulai jam berapa?

rows.en: Could you tell me how much this bag costs?
rows.id: Bisa tolong beri tahu saya harga tas ini berapa?

rows.en: Do you know when the package arrived?
Do you know if the shop is open?
I'd like to know whether the price includes tax.
rows.id: Saya ingin tahu apakah harganya sudah termasuk pajak.

blocks.text:
Two common mistakes:
- *Do you know what time **does** it start?* ✗ → *Do you know what time **it starts**?* ✓ (no second helper)
- *Do you know **is** the shop open?* ✗ → *Do you know **if** the shop is open?* ✓ (a yes/no question needs if)

id.text:
Dua kesalahan yang sering terjadi:
- *Do you know what time **does** it start?* ✗ → *Do you know what time **it starts**?* ✓ (tanpa kata bantu kedua)
- *Do you know **is** the shop open?* ✗ → *Do you know **if** the shop is open?* ✓ (pertanyaan ya/tidak butuh if)

options: Do you know where did Budi park?
Do you know where Budi parked?
Do you know where Budi park?
blocks.explain: Where did Budi park? → did disappears and the verb goes into the past: where Budi parked. 'where did Budi park' keeps the helper, and 'where Budi park' loses the past.

id.explain: Where did Budi park? → did hilang dan kata kerjanya menjadi lampau: where Budi parked. 'where did Budi park' masih memakai kata bantu, dan 'where Budi park' kehilangan bentuk lampaunya.

id.title: Tanpa do/does/did, dan if untuk pertanyaan ya/tidak

material.title: Question tags: not one tag for everything

blocks.text:
A **question tag** is a mini question at the end of a sentence: *You're from Jakarta, **aren't you**?* It works like Indonesian **…, kan?** or **…, ya?**: you say something you think is true and ask the other person to confirm.

The big difference: Indonesian uses the same *kan?* for every sentence. English **builds the tag from the sentence**, in three steps:
- Find the **helper verb**: the small verb that makes questions and negatives (*am/is/are, do/does/did, can, will*). If the sentence has no helper, use **do/does/did**, just like in a question: *She works* → *does*; *You went* → *did*.
- **Flip** it: positive sentence → negative tag (*is → isn't*); negative sentence (with *not / n't*) → positive tag (*doesn't → does*).
- Add a **pronoun** (*I, you, he, she, it, we, they*), never a name: *Rina is a nurse, isn't **she**?*

id.text:
**Question tag** adalah pertanyaan mini di akhir kalimat: *You're from Jakarta, **aren't you**?* Fungsinya seperti **…, kan?** atau **…, ya?** dalam bahasa Indonesia: kamu mengatakan sesuatu yang kamu kira benar, lalu meminta lawan bicara memastikannya.

Bedanya besar: bahasa Indonesia memakai *kan?* yang sama untuk semua kalimat. Bahasa Inggris **membentuk tag dari kalimatnya**, dalam tiga langkah:
- Cari **kata kerja bantu**: kata kerja kecil yang dipakai untuk membuat pertanyaan dan kalimat negatif (*am/is/are, do/does/did, can, will*). Kalau kalimatnya tidak punya kata bantu, pakai **do/does/did**, sama seperti saat membuat pertanyaan: *She works* → *does*; *You went* → *did*.
- **Balik**: kalimat positif → tag negatif (*is → isn't*); kalimat negatif (ada *not / n't*) → tag positif (*doesn't → does*).
- Tambahkan **kata ganti** (*I, you, he, she, it, we, they*), bukan nama: *Rina is a nurse, isn't **she**?*

rows.en: You're from Jakarta, aren't you?
She doesn't eat meat, does she?
You went to Bali last month, didn't you?
rows.id: Kamu ke Bali bulan lalu, kan?

id.note: went: tanpa kata bantu → did → didn't

rows.en: Pak Hasan can drive, can't he?
It will rain later, won't it?
I'm late, aren't I?

blocks.text:
The Indonesian trap: *kan?* fits every sentence, but **isn't it?** doesn't. It only fits sentences with *it is* (or *this/that is*). *You're from Jakarta, isn't it?* ✗ → *aren't you?* ✓, because the sentence has **are** and **you**.

One exception to remember: **I am → aren't I?** (*I'm right, aren't I?*). There is no *amn't I*. The negative is regular: *I'm not late, am I?*

In relaxed speech people also say **right?** after any sentence (*You're from Jakarta, right?*). It's fine with friends, but learn the real tags too: you'll hear them everywhere.

id.text:
Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *kan?* cocok untuk semua kalimat, tapi **isn't it?** tidak. Tag itu hanya cocok untuk kalimat dengan *it is* (atau *this/that is*). *You're from Jakarta, isn't it?* ✗ → *aren't you?* ✓, karena kalimatnya punya **are** dan **you**.

Satu pengecualian yang harus dihafal: **I am → aren't I?** (*I'm right, aren't I?*). Tidak ada *amn't I*. Bentuk negatifnya biasa saja: *I'm not late, am I?*

Dalam obrolan santai, orang juga bilang **right?** setelah kalimat apa pun (*You're from Jakarta, right?*). Itu boleh dengan teman, tapi pelajari juga tag yang sebenarnya: kamu akan sering mendengarnya.

blocks.prompt: Rina and Sari work at the same hospital, ___
blocks.explain: work has no helper, so use do (Rina and Sari = they, so do, not does). Positive sentence → negative tag: don't they?

id.prompt: Pilih tag yang tepat: Rina and Sari work at the same hospital, ___
id.explain: work tidak punya kata bantu, jadi pakai do (Rina and Sari = they, jadi do, bukan does). Kalimat positif → tag negatif: don't they?

id.title: Question tag: tidak ada satu tag untuk semua

blocks.text:
The two tools do different jobs:
- **Indirect questions** are for **strangers** and **formal** situations: a hotel, an airport, a bank, a job interview, a client. *Excuse me, could you tell me…?* sounds much softer than a bare *Where is…?*.
- **Question tags** are for **checking** something you think is true (*The meeting is at ten, isn't it?*) and for keeping a friendly chat going, for example with a new colleague (*It's really hot today, isn't it?*).

**Intonation** means how your voice goes up or down. If your voice goes **down** on the tag, you're quite sure and you just want the other person to agree. If it goes **up**, you're not sure: it's a real question.

id.text:
Dua alat ini punya tugas yang berbeda:
- **Indirect question** untuk **orang yang tidak dikenal** dan situasi **formal**: hotel, bandara, bank, wawancara kerja, klien. *Excuse me, could you tell me…?* terdengar jauh lebih halus daripada *Where is…?* saja.
- **Question tag** untuk **memastikan** sesuatu yang kamu kira benar (*The meeting is at ten, isn't it?*) dan supaya obrolan tetap ramah dan berjalan, misalnya dengan rekan kerja baru (*It's really hot today, isn't it?*).

**Intonasi** adalah naik-turunnya nada suaramu. Kalau nadamu **turun** di tag, kamu cukup yakin dan hanya ingin lawan bicara setuju. Kalau nadamu **naik**, kamu tidak yakin: itu pertanyaan sungguhan.

rows.en: Excuse me, could you tell me where the check-in counter is?
rows.id: Permisi, bisa tolong beri tahu saya konter check-in di mana?

rows.en: Do you know if Pak Hasan is free this afternoon?
rows.id: Kamu tahu apakah Pak Hasan kosong siang ini?

rows.en: It's really hot today, isn't it?
The meeting starts at ten, doesn't it?
rows.note: checking: voice goes up if you're not sure

id.note: memastikan: nada naik kalau kamu tidak yakin

rows.en: You don't eat meat, do you? — No, I don't.
rows.id: Kamu nggak makan daging, kan? — Iya, nggak.

blocks.text: How to answer a tag: answer about the **facts**, not about the speaker. *You don't eat meat, do you?* If you don't eat meat, say ***No**, I don't.* In Indonesian you'd say *Iya* (= betul, saya nggak makan), but in English *Yes* would mean you **do** eat meat.

id.text: Cara menjawab tag: jawab sesuai **fakta**, bukan sesuai kalimat lawan bicara. *You don't eat meat, do you?* Kalau kamu memang tidak makan daging, jawab ***No**, I don't.* Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *Iya* (= betul, saya nggak makan), tapi dalam bahasa Inggris *Yes* berarti kamu **makan** daging.

blocks.prompt: You're new at the office. You want to start a friendly chat with a colleague in the lift. Which is best?
options: It's a busy day today, isn't it?
Tell me if it's a busy day.
It's a busy day today, aren't you?
blocks.explain: A tag invites the other person to agree and starts a chat. The sentence has it is, so the tag is isn't it? 'Tell me…' sounds like an order. (lift is British; Americans say elevator.)

id.prompt: Kamu karyawan baru. Kamu ingin memulai obrolan ramah dengan rekan kerja di lift. Mana yang paling tepat?
id.explain: Tag mengajak lawan bicara setuju dan memulai obrolan. Kalimatnya punya it is, jadi tagnya isn't it? 'Tell me…' terdengar seperti perintah. (lift = bahasa Inggris Britania; di Amerika elevator.)

When do I use if and when do I use whether?
Why is it 'aren't I' and not 'amn't I'?

id.intro: Selamat datang! Hari ini kamu belajar dua alat kecil yang membuat bahasa Inggrismu terdengar sopan dan alami: indirect question (Could you tell me where the station is?) dan question tag (You're from Jakarta, aren't you?). Pemanasan: bagaimana kamu bertanya dengan sangat sopan kepada orang yang tidak dikenal di stasiun, di mana toiletnya?
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'where the station is' dan bukan 'where is the station'?
Kapan pakai if dan kapan pakai whether?
Boleh nggak aku bilang 'right?' saja, bukan question tag?

assessment.iqt-1: Ubah pertanyaan ini menjadi lebih sopan. Mulai dengan 'Could you tell me': Where is the bus stop?
assessment.iqt-2: Ubah pertanyaan ini menjadi sopan. Langsung: When did the meeting finish? Lengkapi: Do you know when ___?
assessment.iqt-3: Kamu ingin bertanya: Is Pak Hasan in the office today? Buat menjadi sopan. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: Do you know ___ Pak Hasan is in the office today?
assessment.iqt-4: Tambahkan question tag: Dimas can speak Japanese, ___?
assessment.iqt-5: Tambahkan question tag: I'm on the list for the office trip, ___?
assessment.iqt-6: Tambahkan question tag: The KRL to Bogor won't be late today, ___?
assessment.iqt-7: Kamu di resepsionis sebuah hotel di Yogyakarta. Tanyakan dengan sopan kepada resepsionis jam berapa sarapan dimulai, dalam bahasa Inggris. Mulai dengan 'Could you tell me'.
